subproblem.title: BV Poincaré inequality on the unit cube with an integer median (Simon Ch. 2, 2.7; (31), (32), (35) of 6.5.1)
subproblem.statement: Let m ∈ ℕ, n := m + 1, Q₁ := {y ∈ ℝⁿ : 0 < y_i < 1 for all i} (Euclid (m + 1), Lebesgue measure) and div g := trace of Dg (LinearMap.trace of fderiv). There is c > 0 (depending only on m) such that for every integer-valued u : ℝⁿ → ℝ (u(y) ∈ ℤ for every y) integrable on Q₁ and every V ∈ ℝ with ∫_{Q₁} u·div g ≤ V for every C^∞ map g : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ with compact support, tsupport g ⊆ Q₁ and |g(y)| ≤ 1 for all y, there is β ∈ ℤ with ∫_{Q₁}|u − β| ≤ cV and |β| ≤ 2∫_{Q₁}|u|.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ m : ℕ, ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ (u : Euclid (m + 1) → ℝ) (V : ℝ), (∀ y, ∃ z : ℤ, u y = z) → IntegrableOn u {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1} → (∀ g : Euclid (m + 1) → Euclid (m + 1), ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) g → HasCompactSupport g → tsupport g ⊆ {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1} → (∀ y, ‖g y‖ ≤ 1) → ∫ y in {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}, u y * LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid (m + 1)) (fderiv ℝ g y) ≤ V) → ∃ β : ℤ, ∫ y in {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}, |u y - β| ≤ c * V ∧ |(β : ℝ)| ≤ 2 * ∫ y in {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}, |u y|
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 2, Lemma 2.7 (Poincaré inequality for BV functions on bounded convex sets) and its printed proof (chapter-02.txt, "2.7 Lemma" and "Proof:"), applied on the unit cube with θ = 1/2, together with the choice (31) and the bound (35) of the integer β_F in Simon's proof of the Deformation Theorem 5.1 (parent step 7, (31)–(32), (35)). The printed proof of 2.7 shrinks U to a convex W depending on u; here W is a concentric cube, whose smooth Poincaré constant is bounded by that of the unit cube, so the final constant depends only on n.

Notation. n := m + 1, Q₁ := {y ∈ ℝⁿ : 0 < y_i < 1 for all i} (Euclid (m + 1), Lebesgue measure Lⁿ = volume, Lⁿ(Q₁) = 1), div g := trace of Dg. For δ ∈ [0, 1/4] let Q_δ := (δ, 1 − δ)ⁿ. Let u be integer-valued and integrable on Q₁, and V ∈ ℝ with ∫_{Q₁} u div g ≤ V for every C^∞ map g : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ with compact support in Q₁ and |g| ≤ 1 (hypothesis (H)). Applying (H) to g = 0 gives V ≥ 0; applying it to −g gives |∫_{Q₁} u div g| ≤ V for all such g.

1. Integer median (Simon (31)). F(b) := Lⁿ(Q₁ ∩ {u ≤ b}) is nondecreasing in b ∈ ℤ, tends to 0 as b → −∞ and to 1 as b → +∞ (u is finite everywhere and Lⁿ(Q₁) = 1; continuity of measure). Let β be the least integer with F(β) ≥ 1/2. Then Lⁿ(Q₁ ∩ {u ≤ β}) ≥ 1/2, and since u is integer-valued, {u ≥ β} = Q₁ ∖ {u ≤ β − 1} has measure 1 − F(β − 1) > 1/2. So min{Lⁿ(Q₁ ∩ {u ≥ β}), Lⁿ(Q₁ ∩ {u ≤ β})} ≥ 1/2.

2. The bound |β| ≤ 2∫_{Q₁}|u| (Simon (35)). If β > 0 then |u| ≥ β on {u ≥ β}, so ∫|u| ≥ β·Lⁿ{u ≥ β} ≥ β/2. If β < 0 then |u| ≥ |β| on {u ≤ β}, so ∫|u| ≥ |β|/2. If β = 0 there is nothing to prove.

3. Smooth Poincaré inequality on cubes. For a cube Q of side s and v ∈ C¹ on a neighbourhood of Q̄, with v̄ := Lⁿ(Q)⁻¹∫_Q v: ∫_Q |v − v̄| ≤ n·s·∫_Q |Dv|. Proof: ∫_Q|v − v̄| ≤ Lⁿ(Q)⁻¹∫_Q∫_Q|v(x) − v(y)| dx dy. Write v(x) − v(y) = Σ_{i=1}^n [v(w^{i−1}) − v(w^i)] with w^i := (y_1, …, y_i, x_{i+1}, …, x_n), and |v(w^{i−1}) − v(w^i)| ≤ ∫ over the segment between x_i and y_i of |∂_i v|. Integrating over x, y ∈ Q (Fubini) bounds the i-th term by s·Lⁿ(Q)·∫_Q|∂_i v|. Summing over i gives the claim. Consequently, for every β' with min{Lⁿ(Q ∩ {v ≥ β'}), Lⁿ(Q ∩ {v ≤ β'})} ≥ θLⁿ(Q) (0 < θ ≤ 1): if β' ≥ v̄ then v − v̄ ≥ β' − v̄ ≥ 0 on {v ≥ β'}, so (β' − v̄)θLⁿ(Q) ≤ ∫_Q|v − v̄|; symmetrically if β' < v̄; hence ∫_Q|v − β'| ≤ ∫_Q|v − v̄| + |v̄ − β'|Lⁿ(Q) ≤ (1 + θ⁻¹)∫_Q|v − v̄|. The same two statements hold, with the same proofs, for v ∈ L¹(Q) in place of a C¹ function when the right side ∫|Dv| is replaced by the limit used in step 5.

4. Shrinking (as in the printed proof). Choose δ ∈ (0, 1/4] so small that Lⁿ(Q₁ ∖ Q_δ) ≤ 1/4 and ∫_{Q₁∖Q_δ}|u − β| ≤ ½∫_{Q₁}|u − β| (absolute continuity of the integral). Then, with W := Q_δ (a cube of side s := 1 − 2δ ≤ 1 and Lⁿ(W) ≤ 1): Lⁿ(W ∩ {u ≥ β}) ≥ 1/2 − 1/4 ≥ ¼Lⁿ(W), likewise for {u ≤ β}, and ∫_{Q₁}|u − β| ≤ 2∫_W|u − β|.

5. Mollification (Simon Ch. 2, 2.5). Let φ be a symmetric mollifier and u_ε := φ_ε ∗ (u·1_{Q₁}) for 0 < ε < δ. On a neighbourhood of W̄, u_ε is C^∞, and u_ε → u in L¹(W) as ε ↓ 0. For every C^∞ g with compact support in W and |g| ≤ 1, ∫_W Du_ε·g = −∫ u_ε div g = −∫ u div(φ_ε ∗ g) ≤ V, because φ_ε ∗ g is C^∞ with compact support in Q₁ (ε < δ) and |φ_ε ∗ g| ≤ 1, and (H) applies to −(φ_ε ∗ g). Taking the supremum over such g (|Du_ε| is continuous, so ∫_W|Du_ε| is the supremum of ∫_W Du_ε·g over C^∞ compactly supported g with |g| ≤ 1, by approximating Du_ε/|Du_ε| truncated) gives ∫_W|Du_ε| ≤ V.
 By step 3 on W: ∫_W|u_ε − ū_ε| ≤ n·s·V ≤ nV, where ū_ε := Lⁿ(W)⁻¹∫_W u_ε → ū := Lⁿ(W)⁻¹∫_W u. Letting ε ↓ 0 (L¹ convergence): ∫_W|u − ū| ≤ nV.

6. Median replacement and conclusion (Simon 2.7 with θ = 1/4 on W, then (32)). By step 4, β satisfies min{Lⁿ(W ∩ {u ≥ β}), Lⁿ(W ∩ {u ≤ β})} ≥ ¼Lⁿ(W), so the argument of step 3 (applied to u ∈ L¹(W) and its mean ū) gives ∫_W|u − β| ≤ (1 + 4)∫_W|u − ū| ≤ 5nV. Hence ∫_{Q₁}|u − β| ≤ 2∫_W|u − β| ≤ 10nV.

So the statement holds with c := 10n = 10(m + 1) > 0, which depends only on m, and the integer β of step 1, which also satisfies |β| ≤ 2∫_{Q₁}|u| by step 2. ∎
proof_key_steps: The least integer β with Lⁿ{u ≤ β} ≥ 1/2 is an integer median: both {u ≥ β} and {u ≤ β} have measure ≥ 1/2, which gives |β| ≤ 2∫|u|.
Smooth L¹ Poincaré inequality on cubes, ∫|v − v̄| ≤ n·s·∫|Dv|, by coordinate paths, and replacement of the mean by any θ-median with factor 1 + θ⁻¹.
Shrink to a concentric cube W = Q_δ keeping half of ∫|u − β| and the median property with θ = 1/4; mollify (supports stay in Q₁) to get ∫_W|Du_ε| ≤ V; pass to the limit.
Conclude ∫_{Q₁}|u − β| ≤ 2·5·n·V, i.e. c = 10n.

audit.reason: The type matches the distributional variation hypothesis and integer-median conclusion. Testing with zero and opposite vector fields supplies nonnegativity and two-sided control. The median, shrinking, mollification and coordinate-path estimates prove both bounds with c = 10(m + 1).

subproblem.title: Dilation push-forward x ↦ λx on currents in ℝ^P: algebra, mass scaling, integrality, ∂, supports, explicit action and the Hᵏ change of variables
subproblem.statement: Conventions: ℝ^P = Euclid P and Hᵈ = μHE[d]. For U ⊆ ℝ^P, 𝒟^d(U) = TestFormOn U d (smooth d-forms on ℝ^P with compact support contained in U) and 𝒟_d(U) = GeometricCurrentOn U d; ∂X = X.boundary (∂X(ω) = X(dω)); X − Y is the contract subtraction (pointwise on test forms). For G ⊆ ℝ^P, M_G(X) = X.massOn G is the supremum of max(X(ω), 0) over ω ∈ 𝒟^d(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ G and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x, where |·| is the Euclidean coefficient norm of covectors (covectorEuclideanNorm); M(X) = X.mass = M_U(X). An IMRep R = (M, θ, ξ) in U is the contract structure IMRep U d; R represents X when X(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHᵈ for every ω ∈ 𝒟^d(U), where ⟨ω, ξ⟩(x) = ξ(x)(ω(x)); μ_R = θ·Hᵈ⌞M is R.measure and R.action(β) = ∫_M θ ξ(β) dHᵈ for any d-form β; X is integer multiplicity (IM, IsIntegerMultiplicity X) if some IMRep represents it. X vanishes off a set E if X(ω) = 0 for every ω whose tsupport is disjoint from E. For every P ∈ ℕ there is an operation dil assigning to every k ∈ ℕ, λ ∈ ℝ and X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^P) (domain univ) a current dil_k(λ, X) ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^P) such that for every k and every λ > 0: (1) dil_k(λ, X − Y) = dil_k(λ, X) − dil_k(λ, Y); (2) dil_k(λ⁻¹, dil_k(λ, X)) = X; (3) M(dil_k(λ, X)) = λ^k·M(X); (4) dil_k(λ, X) is IM whenever X is; (5) ∂dil_{k+1}(λ, X) = dil_k(λ, ∂X) for X ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(ℝ^P); (6) if X vanishes off E then dil_k(λ, X) vanishes off λE = {λx : x ∈ E}; (7) for every X and ω ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^P) there is η ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^P) with η(x) = λ^k ω(λx) for all x and dil_k(λ, X)(ω) = X(η); (8) for every A ⊆ ℝ^P and g : ℝ^P → ℝ, ∫_{λA} g dHᵏ = λ^k ∫_A g(λx) dHᵏ(x). (dil_k(λ, ·) is the push-forward by x ↦ λx, Simon's change of scale between 5.1 and 5.3.)

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the change of scale used by Simon to obtain the scaled Deformation Theorem 5.3 from 5.1 ("obtained from the above by first changing scale x → ρ⁻¹x, then applying 5.1, then changing scale back by x → ρx", chapter-06.txt before 5.3), i.e. the push-forward 2.23 by the proper linear map x ↦ λx, with Remark 2.24(1) (∂ commutes with push-forward), the push-forward of integer multiplicity currents 3.3/3.9 for this injective linear map, and the scaling of Hausdorff measure. This is the tool of step 9 of the parent proof. Accepted DAG theorems named below (imrep_univ_smul_rescale_exists, imrep_smul_rescale_action_measure, dtc_hausdorff_dilation, dtc_approxTangent_dilation) are not siblings of this node: they may be reused as children if this node is decomposed; otherwise the arguments given here are formalized directly.

Notation. All currents and test forms are on univ in ℝ^P. For λ > 0 write δ_λ(x) := λx. For a k-form ω let (δ_λ^#ω)(x) := ω(λx) ∘ (λ·id) (pull-back, Simon 6.1.13), i.e. (δ_λ^#ω)(x)(v_1, …, v_k) = ω(λx)(λv_1, …, λv_k) = λ^k ω(λx)(v_1, …, v_k); so δ_λ^#ω = λ^k ω(λ·) (as a covector-valued map, λ^k • ω(λ • x)). |·| is the Euclidean coefficient norm.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, proof of the Deformation Theorem 5.1, displays (1)–(7) (chapter-06.txt, "Proof of the Deformation Theorem" up to (7)); step 2 of the parent proof. The printed argument uses only that M(T⌞·) and M(∂T⌞·) are finite Borel measures, so it is stated here for two arbitrary finite Borel measures μ, μ' on ℝ^P (in the parent, μ = μ_T and μ' = μ_∂T, the measures of IMReps of T and ∂T).

Notation. n := m + 1 < P, ℓ := P − n ≥ 1. For an index set J ⊆ {0, …, P − 1} with |J| = n + 1 (there are N := binom(P, n + 1) such J) let S_J := span{e_i : i ∈ J} (an (n + 1)-dimensional coordinate subspace, Simon's S_j), p_J the orthogonal projection onto S_J (p_J(x)_i = x_i for i ∈ J, 0 otherwise), Z_J := ℤ^P ∩ S_J (integer vectors vanishing off J), q := (1/2, …, 1/2), x_J := p_J(q). ω_d := L^d(B_1(0)) and B_σ(g) denotes an open ball (in S_J when g ∈ S_J). For a ∈ ℝ^P, L*(a) := {w : w_i − a_i ∈ ℤ for at least n + 1 indices} is the set written in the statement and d_a := infDist(·, L*(a)).

1. Tube description. For every a and r > 0: {x : d_a(x) < r} = ⋃_J ⋃_{z∈Z_J} p_J⁻¹(B_r(p_J(a) + z)). Indeed L*(a) = ⋃_J ⋃_{z∈Z_J} A_{J,z} with A_{J,z} := {w : w_i = a_i + z_i for i ∈ J} = p_J⁻¹(p_J(a) + z) (a point with at least n + 1 coordinates in a_i + ℤ has such coordinates on some (n + 1)-set J), and dist(x, A_{J,z}) = |p_J(x) − p_J(a) − z| (the nearest point of A_{J,z} changes only the J-coordinates). d_a(x) < r iff some w ∈ L*(a) has |x − w| < r iff some A_{J,z} has dist(x, A_{J,z}) < r. In particular this set is open (so measurable).

2. Bad sets have small measure (Simon (1)–(4)). Fix β > 0 (chosen in step 4) and a finite Borel measure ν on ℝ^P. For each J let B_J(ν) be the set of g ∈ S_J with |g − x_J| < 1/4 for which some σ ∈ (0, 1/4) has ν(⋃_{z∈Z_J} p_J⁻¹(B_σ(g + z))) > βσ^{n+1}ν(ℝ^P). Claim: the outer (n + 1)-dimensional Lebesgue measure of B_J(ν) in S_J is at most 5^{n+1}ω_{n+1}β⁻¹; more precisely B_J(ν) ⊆ ⋃_k B_{5σ_k}(b_k) for countably many balls in S_J with Σ_k σ_k^{n+1} ≤ β⁻¹.
 If ν(ℝ^P) = 0, B_J(ν) = ∅. Otherwise choose for each b ∈ B_J(ν) a radius σ_b ∈ (0, 1/4) as in the definition. By the 5-times covering lemma (Simon Ch. 1, 3.4; Mathlib Vitali.exists_disjoint_subfamily_covering_enlargement applied to the balls B_{σ_b}(b) in S_J, radii bounded by 1/4) there is a pairwise disjoint subfamily {B_{σ_k}(b_k)}, countable because S_J is separable and the balls are open and disjoint, with B_J(ν) ⊆ ⋃_k B_{5σ_k}(b_k). The sets p_J⁻¹(B_{σ_k}(b_k + z)) (k, z ∈ Z_J) are pairwise disjoint: for the same z they are preimages of disjoint balls; for z ≠ z', |(b_k + z) − (b_{k'} + z')| ≥ |z − z'| − |b_k − b_{k'}| > 1 − 1/2 > σ_k + σ_{k'}, since b_k, b_{k'} ∈ B_{1/4}(x_J) and σ < 1/4. Summing the defining inequalities over k gives βν(ℝ^P)Σ_kσ_k^{n+1} ≤ Σ_k ν(⋃_z p_J⁻¹(B_{σ_k}(b_k + z))) ≤ ν(ℝ^P), so Σ_kσ_k^{n+1} ≤ β⁻¹ and L^{n+1}(⋃_k B_{5σ_k}(b_k)) ≤ Σ_k ω_{n+1}(5σ_k)^{n+1} ≤ 5^{n+1}ω_{n+1}β⁻¹.

3. Fubini (Simon (5)). With S_J^⊥ := span{e_i : i ∉ J} ((ℓ − 1)-dimensional; ℝ^P = S_J × S_J^⊥ isometrically, Lebesgue measure being the product), {a ∈ B_{1/4}(q) : p_J(a) ∈ B_J(ν)} ⊆ {a : p_J(a) ∈ ⋃_k B_{5σ_k}(b_k), |p_J^⊥(a − q)| < 1/4}, an open set of L^P-measure ≤ 5^{n+1}ω_{n+1}β⁻¹·ω_{ℓ−1}4^{1−ℓ} (for ℓ = 1, S_J^⊥ = {0} and the factor is 1).

4. Choice of a (Simon (5)–(7)). Choose β = β(P, m) > 0 so large that 2N·5^{n+1}ω_{n+1}ω_{ℓ−1}4^{1−ℓ}β⁻¹ < ω_P4^{−P} = L^P(B_{1/4}(q)). By steps 2–3 applied to ν = μ and ν = μ', the union over J of {a ∈ B_{1/4}(q) : p_J(a) ∈ B_J(μ) ∪ B_J(μ')} has outer measure < L^P(B_{1/4}(q)), so some a ∈ B_{1/4}(q) avoids it. For every J, p_J(a) ∈ S_J and |p_J(a) − x_J| = |p_J(a − q)| ≤ |a − q| < 1/4, so p_J(a) ∉ B_J(μ) means: for all σ ∈ (0, 1/4), μ(⋃_{z∈Z_J} p_J⁻¹(B_σ(p_J(a) + z))) ≤ βσ^{n+1}μ(ℝ^P); likewise for μ'. Also |a_i − 1/2| ≤ |a − q| < 1/4 for every i.

5. Conclusion (Simon (6), (7)). Let C := Nβ (a nonnegative real, regarded in ℝ≥0). For r ∈ (0, 1/4), step 1 and subadditivity give μ({d_a < r}) ≤ Σ_J μ(⋃_z p_J⁻¹(B_r(p_J(a) + z))) ≤ Nβr^{n+1}μ(ℝ^P), and the same for μ'. For r = 1/4: {d_a < 1/4} is the increasing union of the sets {d_a < 1/4 − 1/j} (j ≥ 5), so by continuity from below μ({d_a < 1/4}) = lim_j μ({d_a < 1/4 − 1/j}) ≤ lim_j Nβ(1/4 − 1/j)^{n+1}μ(ℝ^P) = Nβ(1/4)^{n+1}μ(ℝ^P), and likewise for μ'. Since n + 1 = m + 2 and C·ENNReal.ofReal(r^{m+2})·μ(univ) = Nβr^{n+1}μ(ℝ^P), both inequalities of the statement hold for every r ∈ (0, 1/4]. C depends only on P and m. ∎

For each J the bad set of g ∈ S_J ∩ B_{1/4}(x_J) violating the β-bound at some radius is covered (5-times covering lemma) by balls B_{5σ_k}(b_k) with Σσ_k^{n+1} ≤ β⁻¹, using disjointness of the translated cylinders.
Fubini bounds the set of a ∈ B_{1/4}(q) with p_J(a) bad; for β = β(P, m) large the 2N exceptional sets do not exhaust B_{1/4}(q).
A good a satisfies μ({d < r}) ≤ Nβr^{n+1}μ(ℝ^P) for r < 1/4 (and r = 1/4 by continuity from below), likewise for μ'; C := Nβ.

subproblem.title: Weak continuity of pulled-back k-forms under uniform convergence of uniformly Lipschitz maps (identification of Simon 2.29 with 3.6)
subproblem.statement: Let k, N' ∈ ℕ, A ⊆ ℝᵏ (Euclid k, Lebesgue measure) measurable, w : ℝᵏ → ℝ integrable on A, L ∈ ℝ≥0, H_j, H : ℝᵏ → ℝ^{N'} (Euclid N') L-Lipschitz maps with H_j → H uniformly on ℝᵏ, and ω ∈ 𝒟ᵏ(ℝ^{N'}) (TestFormOn univ k). Then ∫_A w(u)·ω(H_j(u))(DH_j(u)e_1, …, DH_j(u)e_k) du → ∫_A w(u)·ω(H(u))(DH(u)e_1, …, DH(u)e_k) du as j → ∞, where DH(u) := fderiv ℝ H u (it exists for a.e. u by Rademacher) and e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1. (This is the weak continuity of Jacobian minors; it identifies the limit of smooth push-forwards of Simon 2.29 with the area-formula push-forward 3.6 for integer multiplicity currents.)
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (k N' : ℕ) (A : Set (Euclid k)) (w : Euclid k → ℝ) (L : NNReal) (Hs : ℕ → Euclid k → Euclid N') (H : Euclid k → Euclid N') (ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid N')) k), MeasurableSet A → IntegrableOn w A → (∀ j, LipschitzWith L (Hs j)) → LipschitzWith L H → TendstoUniformly Hs H atTop → Tendsto (fun j => ∫ u in A, w u * (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid N') k) (Hs j u) (fun i => fderiv ℝ (Hs j) u (EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ)))) atTop (𝓝 (∫ u in A, w u * (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid N') k) (H u) (fun i => fderiv ℝ H u (EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ)))))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: this is the identification step that the book leaves implicit between Lemma 2.29 (the push-forward f_#T of a current with M and M∂ finite by a Lipschitz map, defined as the limit of push-forwards by smooth maps) and 3.6 (the push-forward of an integer multiplicity current by a Lipschitz map, defined by the area formula); Simon asserts after 3.9 that the definitions agree, and the deformation proof (parent steps 4–5, homotopy formula 2.25 applied to Lipschitz maps) uses both. The argument is the classical weak continuity of Jacobian minors (null Lagrangians) under uniform convergence with bounded Lipschitz constants, written out below; it is used by the sibling dor_lmb_fcd_im_pushforward (its step 5). Departure from the printed text: a gap is filled; no printed argument is replaced.

Notation. k, N' ∈ ℕ; ℝᵏ = Euclid k with Lebesgue measure; e_1, …, e_k its standard basis. For a map H : ℝᵏ → ℝ^{N'} and a k-form ω on ℝ^{N'} put H^#ω(u)(e) := ω(H(u))(DH(u)e_1, …, DH(u)e_k) with DH(u) := fderiv ℝ H u (0 where H is not differentiable). Lipschitz maps are differentiable a.e. (Rademacher, Mathlib LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt), with ‖DH(u)‖ ≤ L there, and u ↦ DH(u) is measurable (Mathlib measurable_fderiv), so all integrands below are measurable, and they are bounded by ‖ω‖L^k|w|, hence integrable on A. Hypotheses: A ⊆ ℝᵏ measurable (compactness is not needed), w ∈ L¹(A), H_j, H L-Lipschitz, H_j → H uniformly on ℝᵏ, ω ∈ 𝒟ᵏ(ℝ^{N'}).

1. Case k = 0. Then H^#ω(u)(e) = ω(H(u)) (a function), ω is uniformly continuous and bounded, so ω(H_j) → ω(H) uniformly and ∫_A w ω(H_j) → ∫_A w ω(H) by dominated convergence (|wω(H_j)| ≤ ‖ω‖|w|). Assume k ≥ 1.

2. Coordinates. Write ω = Σ_I ω_I dy^{I_1} ∧ ⋯ ∧ dy^{I_k} over increasing multi-indices I ⊆ {1, …, N'} with ω_I ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ^{N'}) (ω_I(y) = ω(y)(e'_{I_1}, …, e'_{I_k})). Then H^#ω(u)(e) = Σ_I ω_I(H(u))·det D(H^I)(u), where H^I := (H^{I_1}, …, H^{I_k}) : ℝᵏ → ℝᵏ and D(H^I)(u) is the k × k matrix of partial derivatives (multilinearity and alternation of dy^I ∘ DH(u)). Also |det D(H_j^I)| ≤ L^k a.e.

3. Reduction. For each I: ∫_A w ω_I(H_j) det DH_j^I − ∫_A w ω_I(H) det DH^I = ∫_A w(ω_I(H_j) − ω_I(H)) det DH_j^I + ∫_A φ_I (det DH_j^I − det DH^I), with φ_I := w·ω_I(H)·1_A ∈ L¹(ℝᵏ). The first term is at most L^k sup|ω_I(H_j) − ω_I(H)|·‖w‖_{L¹(A)} → 0 (ω_I is uniformly continuous). For the second, given ε > 0 choose ψ ∈ C_c^∞(ℝᵏ) with ‖φ_I − ψ‖_{L¹} < ε; the error is at most 2L^kε uniformly in j. So it suffices to prove:
 Claim. If v_j, v : ℝᵏ → ℝᵏ are L-Lipschitz and v_j → v uniformly, then ∫ψ det Dv_j → ∫ψ det Dv for every ψ ∈ C_c^∞(ℝᵏ).

4. Proof of the Claim, by induction on the order of minors. For an r × r minor μ (rows a_1 < ⋯ < a_r, columns l_1 < ⋯ < l_r) of the Jacobian matrix we prove: (M_r) ∫ψ μ(Dv_j) → ∫ψ μ(Dv) for every continuous compactly supported ψ (and all such sequences). The Claim is (M_k) for the full determinant. Since |μ(Dv_j)| ≤ r!L^r uniformly, it suffices in (M_r) to take ψ ∈ C_c^∞ (uniform approximation of continuous compactly supported ψ by smooth ones with supports in a fixed compact set).
 (M_1): μ(Dv) = ∂_l v^a. For Lipschitz g and ψ ∈ C_c^∞, ∫ψ ∂_l g = −∫ ∂_lψ g (the a.e. partial derivative of a Lipschitz function is its weak derivative; Mathlib LipschitzWith.integral_lineDeriv_mul_eq). Hence ∫ψ∂_lv_j^a = −∫∂_lψ v_j^a → −∫∂_lψ v^a = ∫ψ∂_lv^a by uniform convergence on spt ψ.
 (M_{r−1}) ⇒ (M_r), r ≥ 2. Expansion of μ along its first row a := a_1: μ(Dv) = Σ_{b=1}^r (−1)^{b+1} ∂_{l_b}v^a · μ_b(Dv), μ_b the (r − 1)-minor with rows a_2, …, a_r and columns l_1, …, l̂_b, …, l_r. For smooth v the Piola identity Σ_b (−1)^{b+1} ∂_{l_b}(μ_b(Dv)) = 0 holds (it is the l_1⋯l_r-coefficient of d(dv^{a_2} ∧ ⋯ ∧ dv^{a_r}) = 0, i.e. symmetry of second derivatives), so μ(Dv) = Σ_b (−1)^{b+1}∂_{l_b}(v^a μ_b(Dv)) (the l_1⋯l_r-coefficient of dv^{a_1} ∧ ⋯ ∧ dv^{a_r} = d(v^{a_1}dv^{a_2} ∧ ⋯ ∧ dv^{a_r})), and integrating by parts
 (∗) ∫ψ μ(Dv) = −Σ_b (−1)^{b+1}∫ ∂_{l_b}ψ · v^a · μ_b(Dv) for ψ ∈ C_c^∞.
 (∗) holds for Lipschitz v: with v_δ := v ∗ φ_δ (componentwise mollification), v_δ → v uniformly and Dv_δ = (Dv) ∗ φ_δ → Dv a.e. and boundedly (Mathlib ContDiffBump.ae_convolution_tendsto_right_of_locallyIntegrable; |Dv_δ| ≤ L), so both sides of (∗) for v_δ converge to those for v by dominated convergence (polynomial expressions in bounded a.e.-convergent entries).
 Now apply (∗) to v_j: ∫ψμ(Dv_j) = −Σ_b(−1)^{b+1}∫∂_{l_b}ψ (v_j^a − v^a) μ_b(Dv_j) − Σ_b(−1)^{b+1}∫ (∂_{l_b}ψ·v^a) μ_b(Dv_j). The first sum is at most C·sup_{spt ψ}|v_j − v| → 0. In the second, ∂_{l_b}ψ·v^a is continuous with compact support, so by (M_{r−1}) it converges to −Σ_b(−1)^{b+1}∫∂_{l_b}ψ v^a μ_b(Dv) = ∫ψμ(Dv) by (∗) for v. This proves (M_r).

5. Conclusion. By steps 3–4 each term of Σ_I converges, so ∫_A w·H_j^#ω(e) → ∫_A w·H^#ω(e); with step 1 this is the statement (the Lean integrand w u * ω(H_j u)(fun i => fderiv ℝ H_j u (e_i)) is exactly w·H_j^#ω(u)(e)). ∎
proof_key_steps: k = 0 is uniform convergence of ω∘H_j; for k ≥ 1 write H^#ω(e) = Σ_I ω_I(H) det D(H^I).
Since ω_I(H_j) → ω_I(H) uniformly and the determinants are bounded by L^k, it suffices to show ∫ψ det Dv_j → ∫ψ det Dv for ψ ∈ C_c^∞ and Lipschitz v_j → v uniformly (density of C_c^∞ in L¹).
Induction on the order r of minors: r = 1 by integration by parts for Lipschitz functions (Mathlib LipschitzWith.integral_lineDeriv_mul_eq).

r ≥ 2: the Piola identity gives ∫ψμ_r(Dv) = −Σ_b ±∫∂_bψ v^a μ_{r−1,b}(Dv) (extended from smooth to Lipschitz v by mollification); uniform convergence of v_j and the induction hypothesis for the continuous weights ∂_bψ v^a conclude.

subproblem.title: Retraction onto the n-skeleton away from the dual skeleton, Lipschitz with constant c/r off the r-tube (Simon 6.5.4, corrected)
subproblem.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ with m + 1 < P. There is c > 0 such that for every a ∈ ℝ^P (Euclid P) with |a_i − 1/2| < 1/4 for all i there is a map ψ : ℝ^P → ℝ^P with the following properties, where L*(a) := {w : there is a finset s of coordinate indices with |s| ≥ m + 2 and w_i − a_i ∈ ℤ for all i ∈ s} (Simon's L_{ℓ−1}(a), ℓ = P − m − 1) and d(x) := infDist x L*(a): (i) for every x with d(x) > 0, ψ(x) lies in the (m+1)-skeleton of the unit cubical grid (there is a finset s with P ≤ m + 1 + |s| and ψ(x)_i ∈ ℤ for i ∈ s) and |ψ(x) − x| ≤ √P; (ii) for every r with 0 < r ≤ 1/4 and all x, y with d(x) ≥ r and d(y) ≥ r, |ψ(x) − ψ(y)| ≤ (c/r)|x − y|. The constant c depends only on P and m (not on a). This is Simon's Lemma 5.4 with the derivative bound (3) in Lipschitz form.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ), m + 1 < P → ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ a : Euclid P, (∀ i, |a i - 1 / 2| < 1 / 4) → ∃ ψ : Euclid P → Euclid P, (∀ x : Euclid P, 0 < infDist x {w : Euclid P | ∃ s : Finset (Fin P), m + 2 ≤ s.card ∧ ∀ i ∈ s, ∃ z : ℤ, w i - a i = z} → (∃ s : Finset (Fin P), P ≤ m + 1 + s.card ∧ ∀ i ∈ s, ∃ z : ℤ, ψ x i = z) ∧ dist (ψ x) x ≤ Real.sqrt P) ∧ ∀ r : ℝ, 0 < r → r ≤ 1 / 4 → ∀ x y : Euclid P, r ≤ infDist x {w : Euclid P | ∃ s : Finset (Fin P), m + 2 ≤ s.card ∧ ∀ i ∈ s, ∃ z : ℤ, w i - a i = z} → r ≤ infDist y {w : Euclid P | ∃ s : Finset (Fin P), m + 2 ≤ s.card ∧ ∀ i ∈ s, ∃ z : ℤ, w i - a i = z} → dist (ψ x) (ψ y) ≤ c / r * dist x y
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, Lemma 5.4 and its printed proof (chapter-06.txt, from "5.4 Lemma" to the end of the proof of (3)), with the erratum recorded in step 1 of the parent proof: the printed proof of the derivative bound (3) by induction on ℓ uses a false "similarity" identity (see step 8 below), so the printed construction of ψ is kept and the bound is proved directly. This is step 1, (1a)–(1g), of the parent proof, restated for the exact statement.

Notation. n := m + 1 < P and ℓ := P − n ≥ 1. C := [0, 1]^P, q := (1/2, …, 1/2). For a ∈ ℝ^P with |a_i − 1/2| < 1/4 for every i (the hypothesis of the statement; this is all the printed proof uses about a ∈ B_{1/4}(q)) we have a_i ∈ (1/4, 3/4), hence dist(a_i, ℤ) > 1/4. L*(a) := {w : w_i − a_i ∈ ℤ for at least n + 1 = m + 2 indices i} (the set written in the statement; it is Simon's L_{ℓ−1}(a) = a + L_{ℓ−1}), D(w) := dist(w, L*(a)) = infDist w L*(a). L_n := {x : x_i ∈ ℤ for at least ℓ = P − n indices i} (the statement's condition ∃ s, P ≤ m + 1 + |s|, x_i ∈ ℤ for i ∈ s). |·| is the Euclidean norm.

1. Skeleta (1a). A point lies in the j-skeleton L_j iff at least P − j of its coordinates are integers (a j-face z + F fixes P − j integer coordinates; conversely fix those coordinates and choose unit intervals containing the others), so L_n is the n-skeleton. L*(a) is the finite union over (n+1)-element index sets J of the closed sets {w : w_i − a_i ∈ ℤ for i ∈ J}; hence it is closed, nonempty (a ∈ L*(a)) and invariant under translations by ℤ^P. For x ∈ C we have |x_i − a_i| < 1, so x_i − a_i ∈ ℤ iff x_i = a_i; thus Λ(a) := C ∩ L*(a) = {x ∈ C : x_i = a_i for at least n + 1 indices}. Also dist(L*(a), L_n) ≥ 1/4: if w ∈ L_n and w' ∈ L*(a), at least ℓ coordinates of w are integers and at least n + 1 coordinates of w' are in a_i + ℤ; as ℓ + n + 1 > P some index i has both, so |w − w'| ≥ |w_i − w'_i| ≥ dist(a_i, ℤ) > 1/4. In particular L_n ∩ L*(a) = ∅.

2. Coordinate ratios (1b). For x ∈ C and each i let δ_i(x) := |x_i − a_i|, h_i(x) := 1 − a_i if x_i ≥ a_i and h_i(x) := a_i if x_i < a_i (the distance from a_i to the end of [0, 1] on the side of x_i), and r_i(x) := δ_i(x)/h_i(x).
 - h_i(x) ∈ (1/4, 3/4), so δ_i ≤ r_i ≤ 4δ_i.
 - r_i(x) ∈ [0, 1]; r_i(x) = 1 iff x_i ∈ {0, 1}; r_i(x) = 0 iff x_i = a_i.
 - r_i depends only on x_i and is piecewise linear with slopes 1/(1 − a_i) and −1/a_i, both of modulus < 4; on the same side of a_i, |r_i(x) − r_i(z)| = |x_i − z_i|/h_i ≤ 4|x_i − z_i|, and on opposite sides r_i(x) + r_i(z) ≤ 4(δ_i(x) + δ_i(z)) = 4|x_i − z_i|. So |r_i(x) − r_i(z)| ≤ 4|x − z|.
 For 1 ≤ k ≤ P let r_(k)(x) be the k-th largest of r_1(x), …, r_P(x) (with multiplicity) and r_(0) := 1. Since r_(k) = max over k-element index sets I of min_{i∈I} r_i, |r_(k)(x) − r_(k)(z)| ≤ max_i |r_i(x) − r_i(z)| ≤ 4|x − z|. Put κ(x) := r_(ℓ)(x) (unrelated to any other κ). Then κ(x) = 0 iff at most ℓ − 1 of the r_i(x) are positive iff x_i = a_i for at least P − ℓ + 1 = n + 1 indices iff x ∈ Λ(a). So κ > 0 on C ∖ Λ(a).

3. The printed construction and its closed form (1c). For a j-face F of C (n + 1 ≤ j ≤ P) with free index set I_F (|I_F| = j), F = {x ∈ C : x_i = e_i for i ∉ I_F} with e_i ∈ {0, 1}. The projection of a onto F is a_F ((a_F)_i = a_i for i ∈ I_F, = e_i otherwise), a relative interior point of F. The printed radial retraction ψ_F : F ∖ {a_F} → ∂F sends x to the point a_F + τ(x − a_F) of ∂F with τ ≥ 1, i.e. τ = 1/max_{i∈I_F} r_i(x): ψ_F(x)_i = a_i + (x_i − a_i)/max_{i'∈I_F} r_{i'}(x) for i ∈ I_F and ψ_F(x)_i = x_i otherwise; max_{I_F} r > 0 iff x ≠ a_F, and ψ_F = id on ∂F. ψ^(j) := ψ_F on F ∖ {a_F} for every j-face F is consistent (distinct j-faces meet only in relative boundaries, where every ψ_F is the identity), and the printed ψ_0 := ψ^(n+1) ∘ ⋯ ∘ ψ^(P) on C ∖ Λ(a).
 Define Φ(x)_i := a_i + (x_i − a_i)/max(r_i(x), κ(x)) for x ∈ C ∖ Λ(a) (well defined since κ(x) > 0).
 Claim A (ψ_0 = Φ on C ∖ Λ(a)). Commentary, not to be formalized: Claim A only identifies Φ with the printed composite map; the formal statement is proved from the closed form Φ alone in steps 4–7. Fix x ∈ C ∖ Λ(a), so r_(k)(x) ≥ κ(x) > 0 for 0 ≤ k ≤ ℓ. For 0 ≤ k ≤ ℓ let y^(k)_i := a_i + (x_i − a_i)/max(r_i(x), r_(k)(x)); then y^(0) = x (as r_i ≤ 1) and y^(ℓ) = Φ(x). It suffices to show, for 0 ≤ k < ℓ, that y := y^(k) is in the domain of ψ^(P−k) and ψ^(P−k)(y) = y^(k+1). Let A := {i : r_i(x) ≥ r_(k)(x)}, so |A| ≥ k. Each y_i − a_i is a positive multiple of x_i − a_i, so h_i(y) = h_i(x) and r_i(y) = r_i(x)/max(r_i(x), r_(k)(x)), which is 1 for i ∈ A and r_i(x)/r_(k)(x) < 1 for i ∉ A. Hence y ∈ C and y_i ∈ {0, 1} exactly for i ∈ A.
 - If |A| > k: then r_(k+1)(x) = r_(k)(x), so y^(k+1) = y. Every (P − k)-face G containing y has a free coordinate in A (y lies in a (P − k)-face obtained by fixing k coordinates in A), so y ∈ ∂G ∖ {a_G} and ψ_G(y) = y; hence ψ^(P−k)(y) = y = y^(k+1).
 - If |A| = k: A indexes the k largest r_i(x) and r_(k+1)(x) = max_{i∉A} r_i(x) > 0 (k + 1 ≤ ℓ). y lies in the relative interior of exactly one (P − k)-face G, with I_G = {1, …, P} ∖ A, and max_{I_G} r(y) = r_(k+1)(x)/r_(k)(x) > 0, so y ≠ a_G. For i ∉ A, ψ_G(y)_i = a_i + (y_i − a_i)r_(k)(x)/r_(k+1)(x) = a_i + (x_i − a_i)/r_(k+1)(x); for i ∈ A, ψ_G(y)_i = y_i = a_i + (x_i − a_i)/r_i(x). Since r_i(x) ≤ r_(k+1)(x) for i ∉ A and r_i(x) ≥ r_(k)(x) ≥ r_(k+1)(x) for i ∈ A, this is y^(k+1).

4. Properties of Φ (1d).
 (i) Φ(C ∖ Λ(a)) ⊆ C ∩ L_n, with Φ(x)_i ∈ {0, 1} for at least ℓ indices: |Φ(x)_i − a_i| = δ_i(x)/max(r_i(x), κ(x)) ≤ δ_i(x)/r_i(x) = h_i(x) when r_i(x) > 0 (and Φ(x)_i = a_i when r_i(x) = 0), with equality when r_i(x) ≥ κ(x); Φ(x)_i − a_i has the sign of x_i − a_i, so Φ(x)_i lies between a_i and the end of [0, 1] on the side of x_i, and equals that end (0 or 1) for the at least ℓ indices with r_i(x) ≥ κ(x) = r_(ℓ)(x).
 (ii) Φ = id on C ∩ L_n (⊆ C ∖ Λ(a) by step 1): such x has at least ℓ coordinates in {0, 1}, so κ(x) = 1 and Φ(x)_i = x_i.
 (iii) If z ∈ ℤ^P and x, x + z ∈ C ∖ Λ(a), then Φ(x + z) = Φ(x) + z: where z_i ≠ 0 we have x_i, x_i + z_i ∈ {0, 1}, so r_i(x + z) = r_i(x) = 1 for those i and r_i(x + z) = r_i(x) for the others; hence κ(x + z) = κ(x), and in the coordinates with z_i ≠ 0, max(r_i, κ) = 1 so Φ(·)_i is the identity there. (This is the printed property ψ_0(z + x) = z + ψ_0(x).)

5. The map ψ. For w ∉ L*(a) choose z ∈ ℤ^P with w − z ∈ C (e.g. z_i := ⌊w_i⌋); then w − z ∉ L*(a) by periodicity, so w − z ∈ C ∖ Λ(a); put ψ(w) := z + Φ(w − z). By (iii) this does not depend on the choice of z. For w ∈ L*(a) put ψ(w) := w (any value would do). If D(x) > 0 then x ∉ L*(a) (closed), and with z as above: ψ(x) = z + Φ(x − z) has at least ℓ coordinates in z_i + {0, 1} ⊆ ℤ by (i), i.e. there is s with |s| ≥ ℓ, P ≤ m + 1 + |s| and ψ(x)_i ∈ ℤ for i ∈ s; and x, ψ(x) ∈ z + C, so dist(ψ(x), x) ≤ diam C = √P. This proves the first conclusion. Also D is ℤ^P-periodic and 1-Lipschitz (Mathlib Metric.lipschitz_infDist_pt).

6. The Lipschitz estimate in a cube (1e).
 Claim B. For x, z ∈ C ∖ Λ(a): |Φ(x) − Φ(z)| ≤ 4√P|x − z|/κ(x). Fix i; put u(w) := w_i − a_i and μ(w) := max(r_i(w), κ(w)) > 0. By step 2, μ is 4-Lipschitz and |u(x) − u(z)| ≤ |x − z|. If r_i(z) > 0 then |u(z)|/μ(z) ≤ |u(z)|/r_i(z) = h_i(z) < 3/4; if r_i(z) = 0 then u(z) = 0. Hence |Φ(x)_i − Φ(z)_i| = |u(x)/μ(x) − u(z)/μ(z)| ≤ |u(x) − u(z)|/μ(x) + (|u(z)|/μ(z))·|μ(z) − μ(x)|/μ(x) ≤ (1 + (3/4)·4)|x − z|/μ(x) ≤ 4|x − z|/κ(x). Summing squares over the P coordinates gives Claim B.
 Claim C. For x ∈ C: D(x) ≤ √(n + 1)·κ(x). Let J be a set of n + 1 indices carrying the n + 1 smallest values δ_i(x), and x* the point with x*_i := a_i for i ∈ J and x*_i := x_i otherwise. Then x* ∈ C has n + 1 coordinates equal to a_i, so x* ∈ Λ(a) ⊆ L*(a). J omits exactly ℓ − 1 indices, so every i ∈ J has δ_i(x) ≤ δ_(ℓ)(x), the ℓ-th largest δ_i(x); as δ_i ≤ r_i for all i, δ_(ℓ)(x) ≤ r_(ℓ)(x) = κ(x). So D(x) ≤ |x − x*| = (Σ_{i∈J} δ_i(x)²)^{1/2} ≤ √(n + 1)·κ(x).
 Put c₁ := 4√(P(n + 1)). By B and C, for x, z ∈ C ∖ L*(a) (so D(x) > 0):
 (3') |Φ(x) − Φ(z)| ≤ c₁|x − z|/D(x).
 c₁ depends only on P and m, not on a.

7. Lipschitz bounds for ψ on ℝ^P (1f).
 (i) If D ≥ τ > 0 at every point of a segment [w, w'], then |ψ(w) − ψ(w')| ≤ (c₁/τ)|w − w'|. The bounded segment meets finitely many cubes z + C, each in a closed sub-segment (convexity). Order all endpoints of these sub-segments along [w, w']: w = w_0, w_1, …, w_K = w'. Each piece [w_k, w_{k+1}] lies in one cube z + C: the cube containing the midpoint of the piece meets the segment in a closed sub-segment whose endpoints are among the w_j, none strictly between w_k and w_{k+1}, so it contains the piece. Since w_k − z, w_{k+1} − z ∈ C ∖ L*(a) and D(w_k − z) = D(w_k) ≥ τ, (3') and step 5 give |ψ(w_k) − ψ(w_{k+1})| = |Φ(w_k − z) − Φ(w_{k+1} − z)| ≤ (c₁/τ)|w_k − w_{k+1}|. Summing over the collinear, ordered pieces gives the claim.
 (ii) Let c := max(2c₁, 1/4 + 2√P) > 0 and r ∈ (0, 1/4]; let D(x), D(y) ≥ r.
 - If |x − y| < r: every point of [x, y] is within |x − y|/2 < r/2 of x or of y, so D > r/2 there (D is 1-Lipschitz); (i) with τ := r/2 gives |ψ(x) − ψ(y)| ≤ (2c₁/r)|x − y| ≤ (c/r)|x − y|.
 - If |x − y| ≥ r: |ψ(x) − ψ(y)| ≤ |x − y| + |ψ(x) − x| + |ψ(y) − y| ≤ |x − y| + 2√P ≤ (1 + 2√P/r)|x − y| ≤ ((1/4 + 2√P)/r)|x − y| ≤ (c/r)|x − y|, using 1 ≤ 1/(4r).
 This is the second conclusion, with c depending only on P and m. ∎

8. Erratum (commentary, not to be formalized: why the printed proof of (3) is replaced). The printed induction passes from x ∈ int C to y := ψ_C(x) in a (P − 1)-face F and asserts dist(y, L)/dist(x, p_F⁻¹(L)) = |y − a|/|x − a| "by similarity", L = L_{ℓ−2}(a_F) the complete periodic lattice of the hyperplane of F. The homothety with centre a_F and ratio |y − a|/|x − a| fixes a_F but not the other lattice points a_F + z, so the identity is false: for P = 3, n = 1, a = (3/10, 1/2, 1/2), x = (129/200, 1/2, 1/4) one gets y = (99/100, 1/2, 0), ratio 2, but dist(y, L) = 31/100 and dist(x, p_F⁻¹(L)) = 69/200. Steps 3–7 avoid the induction; the only comparison between the local arrangement Λ(a) and the full lattice L*(a) they need is Claim C, via the explicit point x* ∈ Λ(a) ⊆ L*(a).
proof_key_steps: For x ∈ C ∖ Λ(a) the ratios r_i(x) = |x_i − a_i|/h_i(x) are 4-Lipschitz, and κ = r_(ℓ) (ℓ-th largest) is positive exactly off Λ(a) = C ∩ L*(a).

Claim A: the printed composite of radial retractions equals Φ(x)_i = a_i + (x_i − a_i)/max(r_i(x), κ(x)); Φ maps into C ∩ L_n, fixes C ∩ L_n and commutes with integer translations, so ψ(w) := z + Φ(w − z) is well defined, lands in L_n and moves points by at most √P.
Claim B: |Φ(x) − Φ(z)| ≤ 4√P|x − z|/κ(x); Claim C: dist(x, L*(a)) ≤ √(n+1)κ(x) via an explicit point of Λ(a); hence (3') |Φ(x) − Φ(z)| ≤ c₁|x − z|/dist(x, L*(a)).
Cutting segments into cube pieces gives the (c₁/τ)-Lipschitz bound on segments with D ≥ τ, and the two-case argument gives (c/r)-Lipschitz on {D ≥ r} with c = max(2c₁, 1/4 + 2√P).

subproblem.statement: Conventions: ℝ^P = Euclid P and Hᵈ = μHE[d]. For U ⊆ ℝ^P, 𝒟^d(U) = TestFormOn U d (smooth d-forms on ℝ^P with compact support contained in U) and 𝒟_d(U) = GeometricCurrentOn U d; ∂X = X.boundary (∂X(ω) = X(dω)); X − Y is the contract subtraction (pointwise on test forms). For G ⊆ ℝ^P, M_G(X) = X.massOn G is the supremum of max(X(ω), 0) over ω ∈ 𝒟^d(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ G and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x, where |·| is the Euclidean coefficient norm of covectors (covectorEuclideanNorm); M(X) = X.mass = M_U(X). An IMRep R = (M, θ, ξ) in U is the contract structure IMRep U d; R represents X when X(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHᵈ for every ω ∈ 𝒟^d(U), where ⟨ω, ξ⟩(x) = ξ(x)(ω(x)); μ_R = θ·Hᵈ⌞M is R.measure and R.action(β) = ∫_M θ ξ(β) dHᵈ for any d-form β; X is integer multiplicity (IM, IsIntegerMultiplicity X) if some IMRep represents it. X vanishes off a set E if X(ω) = 0 for every ω whose tsupport is disjoint from E. Let P, m ∈ ℕ with n := m + 1 < P and L_n := {x : there is a finset s of coordinate indices with P ≤ m + 1 + |s| and x_i ∈ ℤ for i ∈ s} (the n-skeleton of the unit cubical grid). There is c ≥ 0 such that for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P and every IM Q ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (domain univ) that vanishes off L_n ∩ K and has M(∂Q) ≠ ∞, there are a finite set s of pairs p = (z_p, ι_p) ∈ ℤ^P × (Fin n → Fin P), integers β_p (a function β) and Pc ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) such that: ι_p is strictly increasing for p ∈ s; Pc(ω) = Σ_{p∈s} β_p ∫_{F_p} ω(x)(e_{ι_p(0)}, …, e_{ι_p(m)}) dHⁿ(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P), where F_p := {x : z_{p,i} ≤ x_i ≤ z_{p,i} + 1 for i ∈ range ι_p, x_i = z_{p,i} otherwise} is the closed unit n-face of p = (z_p, ι_p) ∈ ℤ^P × (Fin n → Fin P) (the cell latticeFace 1 p of the project's GMT/Ch06/Contract.lean), oriented by e_{ι_p(0)} ∧ ⋯ ∧ e_{ι_p(m)}, e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1; Q − Pc is IM; M(Q − Pc) ≤ c·M(∂Q); Σ_{p∈s}|β_p| ≤ c·M(Q); F_p ⊆ cthickening(√P, K) for p ∈ s; and Q − Pc vanishes off cthickening(√P, K).

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, proof of the Deformation Theorem 5.1, displays (26)–(37) (chapter-06.txt, from "Now let F be a given face of L_n" to (37)), in the form of step 7 of the parent proof: since Q is integer multiplicity, (26)–(28) are read off from an IMRep of Q (using (IMC)(a)) instead of the constancy-theorem argument for general currents, and (33) follows from Hⁿ(L_{n−1}) = 0. Dependencies: (C1) = the reused sibling dor_imrep_massOn_eq_measure_and_support; (IMC) = the reused sibling cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub; CP = the sibling dor_lmb_fcd_cube_poincare (the BV Poincaré inequality with integer median on the unit cube, Simon Ch. 2, 2.7 with (31), (35)).

Notation. n := m + 1 < P. A pair p = (z, ι) ∈ ℤ^P × (Fin n → Fin P) with ι strictly increasing determines the closed unit face F_p := {x : z_i ≤ x_i ≤ z_i + 1 for i ∈ range ι, x_i = z_i otherwise} and the open face F_p° (strict inequalities); e_ι := (e_{ι(0)}, …, e_{ι(m)}) and V_ι := span e_ι. L_n is the statement's set {x : at least P − n coordinates are integers}, L_{n−1} := {x : at least P − n + 1 coordinates are integers}. All currents are on univ; Q is IM, vanishes off L_n ∩ K (K compact) and M(∂Q) < ∞.

1. Face geometry. (a) φ_p(y) := z + Σ_k y_k e_{ι(k)} is an isometric embedding ℝⁿ → ℝ^P with φ_p([0,1]ⁿ) = F_p and φ_p((0,1)ⁿ) = F_p°; μHE[n] is preserved by isometries and equals Lebesgue measure on ℝⁿ (Mathlib Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image and the characterization of μHE[n] on Euclid n), so Hⁿ(F_p) = Hⁿ(F_p°) = 1, Hⁿ(F_p ∖ F_p°) = 0, and ∫_{F_p} f dHⁿ = ∫_{F_p°} f dHⁿ = ∫_{(0,1)ⁿ} f∘φ_p dy for integrable f. (b) Every point of L_n ∖ L_{n−1} lies in exactly one open face F_p° (its non-integer coordinates, exactly n of them, give range ι, and z_i is the integer part of x_i); distinct open faces are disjoint; and L_{n−1} is a countable union of (n − 1)-dimensional faces, each the isometric image of [0,1]^{n−1}, so Hⁿ(L_{n−1}) = 0. (c) diam F_p = √n ≤ √P; F_p is compact; only finitely many faces meet the compact K. (d) L_n ∖ F_p° is closed (it is (F_p ∖ F_p°) ∪ ⋃_{p'≠p} F_{p'}, a locally finite union of closed sets).

2. The measure of Q (parent (C1); Simon (28)). Let R_Q = (M, θ, ξ) be an IMRep of Q and μ_Q := R_Q.measure = θHⁿ⌞M. By (C1), μ_Q(W) = M_W(Q) for open W. Every admissible form for the open set W₀ := ℝ^P ∖ (L_n ∩ K) has tsupport disjoint from L_n ∩ K, so Q vanishes on it and μ_Q(W₀) = M_{W₀}(Q) = 0. Since θ ≥ 1 on M, Hⁿ(M ∖ (L_n ∩ K)) = 0; with 1(b), Hⁿ-almost every x ∈ M lies in F_p° for exactly one p, and then F_p ∩ K ≠ ∅. Also μ_Q(ℝ^P) = μ_Q(K) ≤ ∫_{M∩K}θ dHⁿ < ∞ (local integrability of the IMRep on the compact K), so M(Q) < ∞, and Hⁿ(M ∩ K') < ∞ for every compact K'.

3. Orientation on a face (Simon (26)–(27)). Fix p with F_p ∩ K ≠ ∅ and let M_p := M ∩ F_p° (Borel). By (IMC)(a) (with M_p ⊆ M ⊆ ℝ^P, U = univ, Hⁿ(M ∩ K') < ∞), for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M_p the approximate tangent spaces of M and of M_p at x agree.  Let 𝒫 be the finite set of p with F_p ∩ K ≠ ∅. By step 2 and (27):

4. Variation bound (Simon (28), second part, by the argument of 2.34–2.35).  Claim: for every C^∞ g : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ with compact support in Q₁ and |g| ≤ 1, ∫_{Q₁} u_p div g ≤ M_{V_p}(∂Q).

For any F put Y(F)(ω) := Σ_{x∈M} θ(x)ε(x)ω(F(x)); it is linear in ω and |Y(F)(ω)| ≤ μ_R(ℝ^N)‖ω‖, so Y(F) ∈ 𝒟_0(ℝ^{N'}). For 0-forms F_j^#ω = ω∘F_j, so if F_j → F pointwise then R.action(F_j^#ω) = Σ_x θ(x)ε(x)ω(F_j x) → Y(F)(ω). Integrality: for y ∈ F(M) let c(y) := Σ_{x∈M, F(x)=y} θ(x)ε(x) ∈ ℤ; the finite set M' := {y : c(y) ≠ 0} with multiplicity |c(y)| and orientation sign(c(y))·id is an IMRep (finite sets are Borel, countably 0-rectifiable, and have approximate tangent space {0} at each of their points: the blow-ups of a finite set at one of its points converge to the point mass at 0) whose action is Y(F). Locality: if F = F' H⁰-a.e. on M, i.e. on all of M, then Y(F) = Y(F'). This proves the statement for k = 0. From now on k ≥ 1.

2. Parametrization (Simon 3.1 with Ch. 3, 1.1; cmc B1). There are countably many compact sets B_i ⊆ ℝᵏ, Lipschitz maps G_i : ℝᵏ → ℝ^N and constants κ_i > 0 such that: G_i is differentiable at every u ∈ B_i with DG_i(u) injective; κ_i|u − v| ≤ |G_i(u) − G_i(v)| for u, v ∈ B_i; the sets G_i(B_i) ⊆ M are pairwise disjoint (and Borel); and Hᵏ(M ∖ ⋃_i G_i(B_i)) = 0. This is the accepted DAG theorem dpf_rectifiable_bilipschitz_pieces (Borel pieces), followed by inner regularity: each Borel piece B is, up to an Lᵏ-null set, a countable disjoint union of compact sets, and the image of an Lᵏ-null set under a Lipschitz map is Hᵏ-null (Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le). Its proof: M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝᵏ) with Hᵏ(M₀) = 0 and F_j Lipschitz (CountablyRectifiable); by Rademacher the non-differentiability set of F_j is null and has null image; the image of the critical set {DF_j not injective} is null (area formula, the Jacobian vanishes there; SimonGMT area_image_criticalSet_eq_zero); the remaining set is partitioned with Mathlib exists_partition_approximatesLinearOn_of_hasFDerivWithinAt into Borel pieces on which F_j is bi-Lipschitz (approximation of an injective linear map with constant less than half its co-norm), and pieces are made disjoint inductively (images of Borel sets under injective continuous maps are Borel, Mathlib MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn).

3. Tangent planes of pieces (cmc B2). Let A ⊆ ℝᵏ be compact and G : ℝᵏ → ℝ^N Lipschitz, differentiable on A, with κ|u − v| ≤ |G(u) − G(v)| on A. Then for Lᵏ-a.e. u ∈ A, DG(u) is injective and G(A) has approximate tangent space V := DG(u)(ℝᵏ) at G(u) (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k (G(A)) (G u) V). Proof: let u be a Lebesgue density point of A and a Lebesgue point of 1_A·JG, where JG := |Λ_kDG e| = √det(DGᵀDG). Density gives, for every unit w, points v ∈ A with v − u = tw + o(t), so |DG(u)w| ≥ κ and JG(u) ≥ κ^k > 0. For f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N) with spt f ⊆ B_ρ(0), the injective area formula (SimonGMT injective_area_formula_lipschitz) and the scaling of Hᵏ give ∫_{blowUpMap (G u) t '' G(A)} f dHᵏ = ∫_{ℝᵏ} 1_A(u + tw) f((G(u + tw) − G(u))/t) JG(u + tw) dw. The integrand vanishes for |w| ≥ ρ/κ; on B_{ρ/κ}(0), (G(u + tw) − G(u))/t → DG(u)w uniformly and 1_A(u + t·)JG(u + t·) → JG(u) in L¹; so the integral tends to ∫ f(DG(u)w)JG(u) dw = ∫_V f dHᵏ (area formula for the linear map DG(u)).
 Consequence (B2′). Since Hᵏ(M ∩ K') < ∞ for compact K' (θ ≥ 1, μ_R finite), (IMC)(a) applied to G_i(B_i) ⊆ M shows: for Hᵏ-a.e. x ∈ G_i(B_i), T_xM exists and equals DG_i(u)(ℝᵏ), u = (G_i|B_i)⁻¹(x). At such x the IMRep field `orients` gives a subspace Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M x Q and ξ(x) a unit orientation of Q; approximate tangent spaces are unique (the defining limits determine the measure Hᵏ⌞Q, hence Q; accepted DAG theorem dpf_itt_approxTangentPlane_eq), so Q = DG_i(u)(ℝᵏ). Two unit orientations of the same k-plane differ by a sign, and Λ_kDG_i(u)e/JG_i(u) (the k-vector α ↦ α(DG_i(u)e_1, …, DG_i(u)e_k)/JG_i(u)) is a unit orientation of it; hence there is a Borel s_i : B_i → {1, −1} with
 (B2′) ξ(G_i(u))(α) = s_i(u)·α(DG_i(u)e_1, …, DG_i(u)e_k)/JG_i(u) for Lᵏ-a.e. u ∈ B_i and all α.
 (Preimages of Hᵏ-null subsets of G_i(B_i) under G_i|B_i are Lᵏ-null, because G_i⁻¹ is Lipschitz on G_i(B_i); accepted DAG theorem ptd_piece_image_measurable_ae_pullback.)

4. Transfer to the parameter domains. Put θ_i := θ∘G_i and w_i := θ_i s_i on B_i. Since JG_i ≥ κ_i^k on B_i (step 3), ∫_{B_i}|w_i| du ≤ κ_i^{−k}∫_{B_i}θ_iJG_i du = κ_i^{−k}μ_R(G_i(B_i)) < ∞ (injective area formula). For every bounded Borel k-form γ on ℝ^N, the area formula on each B_i, (B2′) and step 2 give
 R.action(γ) = Σ_i ∫_{B_i} w_i(u)·γ(G_i u)(DG_i(u)e_1, …, DG_i(u)e_k) du,
 the series converging absolutely (term i is at most sup|γ|·μ_R(G_i(B_i)), since |γ(DG_i e)| ≤ |γ|JG_i). For γ := F_j^#ω with F_j C¹: γ(G_iu)(DG_i(u)e) = ω(F_j(G_iu))(DF_j(G_iu)DG_i(u)e) = (H_{ij}^#ω)(u)(e), where H_{ij} := F_j∘G_i is Lipschitz (constant ΛLip G_i) and differentiable on B_i with DH_{ij} = DF_j(G_i·)DG_i (chain rule). So
 (4.1) R.action(F_j^#ω) = Σ_i ∫_{B_i} w_i (H_{ij}^#ω)(e) du, with |term i| ≤ Λ^k‖ω‖μ_R(G_i(B_i)).

5. Weak continuity of pulled-back forms (fills the gap between 2.29 and 3.6). This is the sibling theorem WC = dor_lmb_fcd_jacobian_weak_continuity: if A ⊆ ℝᵏ is measurable, w ∈ L¹(A), H_j, H : ℝᵏ → ℝ^{N'} are L-Lipschitz with H_j → H uniformly on ℝᵏ and ω ∈ 𝒟ᵏ(ℝ^{N'}), then ∫_A w·ω(H_j(u))(DH_j(u)e_1, …, DH_j(u)e_k) du → ∫_A w·ω(H(u))(DH(u)e_1, …, DH(u)e_k) du (derivatives via fderiv, which exist a.e. by Rademacher). It is applied with A := B_i (compact, hence measurable), w := w_i, H_j := F_j∘G_i and H := F∘G_i, which are (Λ·Lip G_i)-Lipschitz with F_j∘G_i → F∘G_i uniformly on ℝᵏ because F_j → F uniformly on ℝ^N; at every u ∈ B_i, D(F_j∘G_i)(u) = DF_j(G_iu)DG_i(u) (chain rule), so its integrand is the integrand of (4.1).

6. The current Y(F) (Simon 3.6). For Λ-Lipschitz F : ℝ^N → ℝ^{N'} let H_i := F∘G_i (Lipschitz, differentiable a.e.) and define
 Y(F)(ω) := Σ_i ∫_{B_i} w_i (H_i^#ω)(e) du.
 At every u ∈ B_i where H_i is differentiable (G_i is differentiable at u), |DH_i(u)v| = lim_{t↓0}|F(G_i(u + tv)) − F(G_i(u))|/t ≤ Λ·lim_{t↓0}|G_i(u + tv) − G_i(u)|/t = Λ|DG_i(u)v|, so |(H_i^#ω)(u)(e)| ≤ ‖ω‖|Λ_kDH_i(u)e| ≤ ‖ω‖Λ^kJG_i(u) and term i is at most Λ^k‖ω‖μ_R(G_i(B_i)). So the series converges absolutely, Y(F) is linear in ω with |Y(F)(ω)| ≤ Λ^k‖ω‖μ_R(ℝ^N), hence sequentially continuous on test forms: Y(F) ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^{N'}). (For non-Lipschitz F put Y(F) := 0.)
 Limit property. Let F_j be C¹, Λ-Lipschitz, F_j → F uniformly. For each i, H_{ij} = F_j∘G_i → H_i uniformly with Lipschitz constants ≤ ΛLip G_i, so by WC (step 5; w = w_i ∈ L¹(B_i), B_i compact) term i of (4.1) converges to term i of Y(F)(ω); all terms are bounded by the summable Λ^k‖ω‖μ_R(G_i(B_i)); by dominated convergence for series, R.action(F_j^#ω) → Y(F)(ω).
 Locality. Let F, F' be Λ-Lipschitz with F = F' Hᵏ-a.e. on M. Then Z_i := {u ∈ B_i : H_i(u) ≠ H'_i(u)} has G_i(Z_i) Hᵏ-null, so Z_i is Lᵏ-null (step 3); at every density point of B_i ∖ Z_i where H_i, H'_i are differentiable (a.e. u ∈ B_i), DH_i(u) = DH'_i(u) (the derivative of a Lipschitz map at a density point of a set is determined by its values on that set). So the integrands agree a.e. and Y(F) = Y(F').

7. Integrality (Simon 3.6–3.9; cmc B3). Fix Λ-Lipschitz F. Let A_i⁺ := {u ∈ B_i : H_i differentiable at u, DH_i(u) injective}. On B_i ∖ A_i⁺ (up to a null set) Λ_kDH_i e = 0, so (H_i^#ω)(e) = 0 there. Apply step 2's partition argument to H_i on A_i⁺: up to an Lᵏ-null set, A_i⁺ is a countable disjoint union of compact A_{il} on which H_i is injective with |H_i(u) − H_i(v)| ≥ κ_{il}|u − v|. Let N_{il} := H_i(A_{il}) (compact), g_{il} := w_i∘(H_i|A_{il})⁻¹ (a nonzero integer, ±θ) and η_{il} := (Λ_kDH_i e/JH_i)∘(H_i|A_{il})⁻¹ (a unit simple k-vector). By step 3 applied to H_i on A_{il}, for Hᵏ-a.e. y ∈ N_{il}, N_{il} has approximate tangent space DH_i(u)(ℝᵏ) at y = H_i(u), which η_{il}(y) orients. Hence (N_{il}, |g_{il}|, sign(g_{il})η_{il}) is an IMRep in univ ⊆ ℝ^{N'} (N_{il} is Borel and countably k-rectifiable as a Lipschitz image of a compact set, extended to ℝᵏ by Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.extend_pi; the multiplicity is a positive integer, Borel, with ∫_{N_{il}}|g_{il}| dHᵏ = ∫_{A_{il}}|w_i|JH_i du < ∞; the orientation is Borel and orients the approximate tangent spaces). Let Φ_{il} be the current it represents (its action is a current: linear, bounded by ‖ω‖∫|g_{il}|). By the injective area formula for H_i on A_{il},
 ∫_{A_{il}} w_i (H_i^#ω)(e) du = ∫_{A_{il}} w_i ⟨ω(H_i u), η_{il}(H_i u)⟩JH_i(u) du = Φ_{il}(ω),
 so Y(F)(ω) = Σ_{i,l} Φ_{il}(ω), absolutely convergent. M(Φ_{il}) ≤ ∫_{N_{il}}|g_{il}| dHᵏ (for admissible ω, |⟨ω, η⟩| ≤ |ω| ≤ 1), and Σ_{i,l}∫_{N_{il}}|g_{il}| = Σ_{i,l}∫_{A_{il}}|w_i|JH_i ≤ Λ^kΣ_i∫_{B_i}θ_iJG_i = Λ^kμ_R(ℝ^N) < ∞ (JH_i ≤ Λ^kJG_i as in step 6). Enumerate the countably many pairs (i, l) by ℕ, padding with zero currents (IM: the IMRep with empty carrier). (IMS), with U = univ (open), degree k = (k − 1) + 1 and these IM currents of summable mass, gives an IM current Y' with Σ_{i,l}Φ_{il}(ω) = Y'(ω) for every ω. Hence Y(F) = Y' (GeometricCurrentOn.ext) is integer multiplicity.

8. Conclusion. The function F ↦ Y(F) of steps 1 and 6 satisfies the three requirements: Y(F) is IM for Λ-Lipschitz F (steps 1, 7); R.action(F_j^#ω) → Y(F)(ω) for every sequence of C¹ Λ-Lipschitz F_j converging uniformly to F and every test form ω (steps 1, 6); and Y(F) = Y(F') when F = F' Hᵏ-a.e. on the carrier (steps 1, 6). ∎
proof_key_steps: k = 0: the carrier is finite and Y(F) = Σ θ(x)ε(x)δ_{F(x)}, an IM 0-current; the limit and locality are immediate.

k ≥ 1: parametrize M up to a null set by compact bi-Lipschitz pieces G_i(B_i); at a.e. u, T_{G_i u}M = DG_i(u)(ℝᵏ) (density-point blow-up with the area formula and (IMC)(a)), so ξ(G_i u) = ±Λ_kDG_i(u)e/JG_i(u).
Transfer: R.action(F_j^#ω) = Σ_i ∫_{B_i} w_i (F_j∘G_i)^#ω(e) du with w_i = θ_i s_i ∈ L¹, absolutely convergent.
The sibling WC (weak continuity of pulled-back forms) passes to the limit term by term; dominated convergence over i gives R.action(F_j^#ω) → Y(F)(ω) := Σ_i ∫ w_i (F∘G_i)^#ω(e).
Locality: equal maps a.e. on M give equal parameter maps a.e. on B_i and equal derivatives at density points.

Integrality: split the injective-derivative part of each B_i into bi-Lipschitz pieces A_il; the area formula writes Y(F) = Σ Φ_il with IM Φ_il = τ(H_i(A_il), |g_il|, ±η_il) of summable mass; (IMS) makes the sum IM.

subproblem.statement: Conventions: ℝ^P = Euclid P and Hᵈ = μHE[d]. For U ⊆ ℝ^P, 𝒟^d(U) = TestFormOn U d (smooth d-forms on ℝ^P with compact support contained in U) and 𝒟_d(U) = GeometricCurrentOn U d; ∂X = X.boundary (∂X(ω) = X(dω)); X − Y is the contract subtraction (pointwise on test forms). For G ⊆ ℝ^P, M_G(X) = X.massOn G is the supremum of max(X(ω), 0) over ω ∈ 𝒟^d(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ G and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x, where |·| is the Euclidean coefficient norm of covectors (covectorEuclideanNorm); M(X) = X.mass = M_U(X). An IMRep R = (M, θ, ξ) in U is the contract structure IMRep U d; R represents X when X(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHᵈ for every ω ∈ 𝒟^d(U), where ⟨ω, ξ⟩(x) = ξ(x)(ω(x)); μ_R = θ·Hᵈ⌞M is R.measure and R.action(β) = ∫_M θ ξ(β) dHᵈ for any d-form β; X is integer multiplicity (IM, IsIntegerMultiplicity X) if some IMRep represents it. X vanishes off a set E if X(ω) = 0 for every ω whose tsupport is disjoint from E. Assume (IMS) the exact frozen statement of dor_lmb_fc_im_series (a resolved dependency of the parent node, not yet accepted, hence taken as an antecedent): for all P, m, every open U ⊆ ℝ^P and IM currents X_r ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(U) (r ∈ ℕ) with Σ_r M(X_r) ≠ ∞ there is an IM Y ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(U) with Σ_r X_r(ω) = Y(ω) (HasSum) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}(U) and M(Y) ≤ Σ_r M(X_r). For every P ∈ ℕ there are operations push_k(F, X) ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^P) and homot_k(F, G, X) ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(ℝ^P) (k ∈ ℕ, F, G : ℝ^P → ℝ^P, X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^P), domain univ) such that, for every k, Λ ∈ ℝ≥0, Λ-Lipschitz F, G, F', G', compact E ⊆ ℝ^P and IM X, Y ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^P) vanishing off E: (1) push_k(id, X) = X; (2) push_k(F, X − Y) = push_k(F, X) − push_k(F, Y) and homot_k(F, G, X − Y) = homot_k(F, G, X) − homot_k(F, G, Y); (3) if F = F' and G = G' on E then push_k(F, X) = push_k(F', X) and homot_k(F, G, X) = homot_k(F', G', X); (4) push_k(F, X) and homot_k(F, G, X) are IM, M(push_k(F, X)) ≤ Λ^k·M(X), push_k(F, X) vanishes off F(E), homot_k(F, G, X) vanishes off {F(x) + t(G(x) − F(x)) : x ∈ E, t ∈ [0, 1]}, and for every δ ∈ ℝ with |F(x) − G(x)| ≤ δ for all x ∈ E, M(homot_k(F, G, X)) ≤ δ(2Λ)^k·M(X) (δ via ENNReal.ofReal); (5) if X ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(ℝ^P) is IM, vanishes off E and ∂X is IM, then ∂push_{k+1}(F, X) = push_k(F, ∂X) and push_{k+1}(G, X) − push_{k+1}(F, X) − homot_k(F, G, ∂X) = ∂homot_{k+1}(F, G, X). (push_k(F, X) = F_#X and homot_k(F, G, X) = h_#([[(0,1)]] × X) for the affine homotopy h(t, x) = F(x) + t(G(x) − F(x)): Simon 2.17–2.29 with 3.2(2), 3.9.)

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, 2.17–2.29 (products 2.17–2.22, push-forward 2.23 and Remark 2.24, the homotopy formula 2.25 and the mass bound 2.27 for affine homotopies, the Lipschitz push-forward 2.29) and 3.2(2), 3.9 (products and push-forwards of integer multiplicity currents), chapter-06.txt lines from "2.17 Definition" to the proof of 2.29 and from "3.2 Remarks" to 3.9; these are the "Results of the book used by the printed proof" listed in the parent proof for steps 4–6 (the operators ψ_# and h_#([[(0,1)]] × ·)). They are specialized to integer multiplicity currents with compact support, which is all the parent uses (every current it pushes forward is IM: restrictions of T and ∂T, slices, and their differences). Integrality is the sibling IPF = dor_lmb_fcd_im_pushforward (Simon 3.6–3.9 with the identification of the limits of 2.29), applied to the antecedent (IMS). Other dependencies: (C1) = the reused sibling dor_imrep_massOn_eq_measure_and_support; (IMC) = the reused sibling cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub. Accepted DAG theorems named below (dpf_rectifiable_bilipschitz_pieces) are not siblings of this node: they may be reused as children if this node is decomposed; otherwise the arguments given here are formalized directly.

Notation. All currents are on univ. A current X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^P) is called admissible if it is IM and vanishes off some compact set. ‖ω‖ := sup_y |ω(y)| (Euclidean coefficient norm). For a C¹ map Φ and a form ω, Φ^#ω(x) := ω(Φ(x)) ∘ DΦ(x) (Lean: (ω (Φ x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ Φ x)). Hadamard's bound |α(v_1, …, v_k)| ≤ |α||v_1|⋯|v_k| (expand α = Σ_I α_I dy^I in the orthonormal basis of increasing coordinate covectors, so α(v) = Σ_I α_I det(v^I); by Cauchy–Schwarz and Cauchy–Binet, |α(v)|² ≤ |α|²Σ_I det(v^I)² = |α|²det(v_i·v_j) ≤ |α|²Π|v_i|², the last step by Hadamard's inequality) and the form of IMRep orientations ((IMC)(d): ξ(x)(α) = ±α(τ) for an orthonormal frame τ of T_xM) give, for an IMRep R and a C¹ Λ-Lipschitz Φ: |R.action(Φ^#ω)| ≤ Λ^k‖ω‖μ_R(ℝ^P)  (★).

1. Admissible currents and their representations. Let X be admissible, vanishing off the compact set E, and R = (M, θ, ξ) an IMRep of X, μ_R := R.measure.
 (a) μ_R(ℝ^P ∖ E) = 0: by (C1), μ_R(W) = M_W(X) for open W, and every admissible form for W := ℝ^P ∖ E has tsupport disjoint from E. Since θ ≥ 1 on M, Hᵏ(M ∖ E) = 0.
 (b) M(X) = μ_R(ℝ^P) = μ_R(E) ≤ ∫_{M∩E}θ dHᵏ < ∞ (C1 and local integrability on the compact E); in particular R satisfies the hypothesis R.measure univ ≠ ∞ of IPF.
 (c) For every bounded Borel k-form γ that equals a test form ζγ' on a neighbourhood of E: R.action(γ) = X(ζγ'), because the integrands agree Hᵏ-a.e. on M by (a). In particular, if ζ ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ^P) equals 1 on a neighbourhood of E and γ is a C^∞ form, R.action(γ) = X(ζγ); and X(ω) = X(ζω) for test forms ω (the difference (1 − ζ)ω has tsupport disjoint from E).
 (d) Canonical data: fix for each admissible X an IMRep R_X, and let E_X := the support of the measure μ_{R_X} (closed). By (a), E_X ⊆ E for every closed E off which X vanishes, so E_X is compact, μ_{R_X}(ℝ^P ∖ E_X) = 0 (Mathlib Measure.measure_compl_support), and X vanishes off E_X (if tsupport ω ∩ E_X = ∅, the integrand θξ(ω) vanishes μ_{R_X}-a.e.). If E_X = ∅ then X = 0.

2. Smooth approximations and the Lipschitz push-forward (Simon 2.23, 2.24(2), 2.29 with 3.9). For a Λ-Lipschitz F : ℝ^P → ℝ^P let F_j := F ∗ φ_{1/j} (componentwise convolution with a standard mollifier): F_j is C^∞, Λ-Lipschitz (|F_j(x) − F_j(y)| ≤ ∫|F(x − z) − F(y − z)|φ_{1/j}(z) dz ≤ Λ|x − y|), and sup|F_j − F| ≤ Λ/j → 0.
 Definition. For admissible X and Lipschitz F, push k F X := Y_{R_X}(F), where Y_{R_X} is the function given by IPF (applied to (IMS) and to R_X); otherwise push k F X := 0.
 Characterization (Char-push). Let X be admissible vanishing off a compact E, F Λ-Lipschitz, F_j any C^∞ Λ-Lipschitz maps with F_j → F uniformly, and ζ ∈ C_c^∞ equal to 1 near E. Then for every test form ω: push k F X (ω) = lim_j R_X.action(F_j^#ω) = lim_j X(ζF_j^#ω). (IPF's limit clause; then 1(c), ζF_j^#ω being a test form.)
 Note: by IPF's limit clause, the value does not depend on Λ (any admissible Λ for F gives the same limit for the mollified sequence).

3. Products (Simon 2.17–2.22, 3.2(2)). Identify ℝ^{P+1} = Euclid (P + 1) with ℝ × ℝ^P (coordinate 0 is t, e_0 its unit vector). For an admissible X with R_X = (M, θ, ξ) define R̂_X := ((0,1) × M, θ∘pr₂, ξ̂) with ξ̂(t, x)(β) := ξ(x)(β₁(t, x)), where for a (k+1)-covector β at (t, x), β₁(v_1, …, v_k) := β(e_0, (0, v_1), …, (0, v_k)) (ξ̂ = e_0 ∧ ξ). Claim: R̂_X is an IMRep of degree k + 1 in univ ⊆ ℝ^{P+1}, μ_{R̂_X}(ℝ^{P+1}) = μ_{R_X}(ℝ^P) < ∞, and for every bounded Borel (k+1)-form β on ℝ^{P+1}: R̂_X.action(β) = ∫_0^1 R_X.action(β₁(t, ·)) dt.
 Proof. (i) Product-null lemma: if Hᵏ(Z) = 0 then H^{k+1}(I × Z) = 0 for every bounded interval I (cover Z by sets C_j with 0 < d_j := max(diam C_j, ε2^{−j}) and Σd_j^k < 2ε, and I × C_j by ⌈|I|/d_j⌉ sets of diameter ≤ √2 d_j; the sum of (diameter)^{k+1} is ≤ c(|I| + 1)Σ_j d_j^k). (ii) Parametrization (Simon 3.1, Ch. 3, 1.1): there are countably many compact B_i ⊆ ℝᵏ, Lipschitz G_i : ℝᵏ → ℝ^P and κ_i > 0 such that G_i is differentiable with injective derivative at every point of B_i, κ_i|u − v| ≤ |G_i(u) − G_i(v)| on B_i, the sets G_i(B_i) ⊆ M are Borel and pairwise disjoint, and Hᵏ(M ∖ ⋃_iG_i(B_i)) = 0. (This is the accepted DAG theorem dpf_rectifiable_bilipschitz_pieces, with Borel pieces, followed by inner regularity: a Borel piece is, up to an Lᵏ-null set whose Lipschitz image is Hᵏ-null (Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le), a countable disjoint union of compact sets. Its proof: M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_jF_j(ℝᵏ) with Hᵏ(M₀) = 0 and F_j Lipschitz; by Rademacher the non-differentiability set of F_j is null and has null image; the image of {DF_j not injective} is null by the area formula (SimonGMT area_image_criticalSet_eq_zero); the rest is cut by Mathlib exists_partition_approximatesLinearOn_of_hasFDerivWithinAt into Borel pieces on which F_j is bi-Lipschitz, and the pieces are made disjoint inductively using Mathlib MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn.) Let JG_i := √det(DG_iᵀDG_i). The maps Ĝ_i(t, u) := (t, G_i(u)) are injective and bi-Lipschitz on (0,1) × B_i with Jacobian JĜ_i(t, u) = JG_i(u); the injective area formula (SimonGMT) gives H^{k+1}⌞((0,1) × G_i(B_i)) = L¹⌞(0,1) ⊗ Hᵏ⌞G_i(B_i), and with (i), H^{k+1}⌞((0,1) × M) = L¹⌞(0,1) ⊗ Hᵏ⌞M. The same holds for (I × A) whenever A is a Borel countably k-rectifiable set with locally finite Hᵏ and I an interval, and for dilates and translates of such sets. (iii) (0,1) × M is Borel and countably (k+1)-rectifiable ((0,1) × G_i(ℝᵏ) ⊆ Ĝ_i(ℝ^{k+1}), plus the null set (0,1) × (M ∖ ⋃ G_i(B_i)) by (i)); θ∘pr₂ is a Borel positive integer on it; ξ̂ is measurable; local integrability and the mass identity follow from (ii) and Fubini. (iv) Tangent planes: let x ∈ M be a point where M has approximate tangent space T_xM (Hᵏ-a.e. x) and t ∈ (0,1). The blow-up of (0,1) × M at (t, x) with scale r is ((0,1) − t)/r × (M − x)/r, so by (ii), for f ∈ C_c(ℝ^{P+1}), ∫_{blow-up} f dH^{k+1} = ∫_{((0,1)−t)/r} ∫_{(M−x)/r} f(s, y) dHᵏ(y) ds → ∫_ℝ ∫_{T_xM} f(s, y) dHᵏ(y) ds = ∫_{ℝe_0 ⊕ T_xM} f dH^{k+1} (for each s by the tangent property of M at x, dominated convergence in s, f having compact support). So (0,1) × M has approximate tangent space ℝe_0 ⊕ T_xM at H^{k+1}-a.e. point, and e_0 ∧ ξ(x) is a unit orientation of it when ξ(x) = ±τ_1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ τ_k orients T_xM (e_0, τ is an orthonormal frame). (v) Fubini with (ii) gives the action formula. (For k = 0, M is finite and (0,1) × M is a finite union of open unit segments; (i)–(v) are immediate.)

4. The homotopy operator. For Λ-Lipschitz F, G and admissible X with E_X ≠ ∅, let χ_X(x) := max(0, 1 − infDist x E_X) (1-Lipschitz, = 1 on E_X, vanishing outside a compact set), c(t) := min(1, max(0, t)), and Ĥ(t, x) := F(x) + c(t)χ_X(x)(G(x) − F(x)). Ĥ is Lipschitz on ℝ^{P+1}: χ_X(G − F) is bounded and Lipschitz (G − F is bounded on the compact set where χ_X ≠ 0), and c is bounded and 1-Lipschitz. Define homot k F G X := Y_{R̂_X}(Ĥ) (IPF applied to (IMS) and to R̂_X, which has finite mass by 3); in all other cases (F or G not Lipschitz, X not admissible, or E_X = ∅, i.e. X = 0) put homot k F G X := 0.
 Characterization (Char-homot). Let X be admissible vanishing off a compact E (so E_X ⊆ E), F, G Λ-Lipschitz, F_j, G_j C^∞ Λ-Lipschitz with F_j → F, G_j → G uniformly (e.g. mollifications), h_j(t, x) := F_j(x) + t(G_j(x) − F_j(x)), and for a k'-form ω (k' = k + 1) the C^∞ k-form
 (K_jω)(x)(v_1, …, v_k) := ∫_0^1 ω(h_j(t, x))(G_j(x) − F_j(x), D_xh_j(t, x)v_1, …, D_xh_j(t, x)v_k) dt, D_xh_j = (1 − t)DF_j + tDG_j
 (the interior product with ∂_t of h_j^#ω, integrated in t). Let ζ ∈ C_c^∞ equal 1 near E. Then homot k F G X (ω) = lim_j R_X.action(K_jω) = lim_j X(ζK_jω).
 Proof. Choose s ∈ C^∞(ℝ), bounded with bounded derivative and s(t) = t on [−1, 2], and χ̃ ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ^P), 0 ≤ χ̃ ≤ 1, χ̃ = 1 on a neighbourhood of E. Ĥ_j(t, x) := F_j(x) + s(t)χ̃(x)(G_j(x) − F_j(x)) are C^∞ and Lipschitz with a constant independent of j (∂_tĤ_j = s'(t)χ̃(G_j − F_j) and D_xĤ_j = DF_j + s(t)(Dχ̃ ⊗ (G_j − F_j) + χ̃(DG_j − DF_j)) are bounded, G_j − F_j being uniformly bounded on spt χ̃), and Ĥ_j → Ĥ' := F + s(t)χ̃(G − F) uniformly. Ĥ' = Ĥ on [0,1] × E_X, which contains H^{k+1}-almost all of the carrier (0,1) × M of R̂_X (1(d)); by IPF's locality clause (with a common Lipschitz constant for Ĥ and Ĥ'), Y_{R̂_X}(Ĥ) = Y_{R̂_X}(Ĥ'), and by its limit clause, homot k F G X (ω) = lim_j R̂_X.action(Ĥ_j^#ω). By the action formula of 3, R̂_X.action(Ĥ_j^#ω) = ∫_0^1 R_X.action((Ĥ_j^#ω)₁(t, ·)) dt, and for t ∈ (0,1) and x near E (where χ̃ ≡ 1, s(t) = t) (Ĥ_j^#ω)₁(t, x) is the integrand of K_jω. Fubini (bounded integrand, finite measure) and 1(c) give the claim.

5. Properties (1)–(3). Let Λ, F, G, F', G' be as in the statement and X, Y admissible, vanishing off the compact E.
 (1) Identity: with F_j := id in (Char-push), push k id X (ω) = lim X(ζω) = X(ζω) = X(ω) (1(c)).
 (2) Linearity: X − Y is IM by (IMC)(c) and vanishes off E, so it is admissible. With a common ζ, F_j, G_j in (Char-push) and (Char-homot), push k F (X − Y)(ω) = lim (X − Y)(ζF_j^#ω) = lim X(ζF_j^#ω) − lim Y(ζF_j^#ω) = (push k F X − push k F Y)(ω), and likewise for homot with ζK_jω.
 (3) Locality: if F = F' on E then F = F' Hᵏ-a.e. on the carrier of R_X (1(a)); IPF's locality clause gives push k F X = push k F' X. If moreover G = G' on E, the two maps Ĥ, Ĥ' of 4 (built with the same χ_X) agree on [0,1] × E_X ⊆ [0,1] × E, which contains H^{k+1}-almost all of the carrier of R̂_X; so homot k F G X = homot k F' G' X.

6. Properties (4): integrality, masses, vanishing (Simon 2.27, 2.29, 3.9).
 - push k F X and homot k F G X are IM by IPF (for X = 0 or E_X = ∅ they are 0, which is IM: empty carrier).
 - Mass of push: by (★) and 1(b), |X(ζF_j^#ω)| = |R_X.action(F_j^#ω)| ≤ Λ^k‖ω‖M(X); in the limit |push k F X (ω)| ≤ Λ^k‖ω‖M(X), so M(push k F X) ≤ Λ^k M(X).
 - Vanishing of push off F(E): F(E) is compact; if tsupport ω is disjoint from it, the two sets have positive distance, so for large j, F_j(E) ∩ tsupport ω = ∅ and F_j^#ω = 0 on E; then R_X.action(F_j^#ω) = 0 by 1(a), and push k F X (ω) = 0.
 - Vanishing of homot off h([0,1] × E) = {F x + t(G x − F x) : x ∈ E, t ∈ [0,1]} (compact): if tsupport ω is disjoint from it then, h_j → h uniformly on [0,1] × E, for large j h_j([0,1] × E) ∩ tsupport ω = ∅, so K_jω = 0 on E and homot k F G X (ω) = lim R_X.action(K_jω) = 0.
 - Mass of homot (Simon 2.27): let δ be such that |F(x) − G(x)| ≤ δ for x ∈ E. If E = ∅ then X = 0, homot k F G X (ω) = lim X(ζK_jω) = 0 and the bound is trivial; otherwise δ ≥ 0. For x ∈ E, ‖D_xh_j‖ ≤ (1 − t)Λ + tΛ = Λ and |G_j(x) − F_j(x)| ≤ δ + ε_j with ε_j := sup|G_j − G| + sup|F_j − F| → 0, so by Hadamard and the form of ξ, |ξ(x)(K_jω(x))| ≤ (δ + ε_j)Λ^k‖ω‖ for Hᵏ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ E, hence |R_X.action(K_jω)| ≤ (δ + ε_j)Λ^k‖ω‖M(X) and |homot k F G X (ω)| ≤ δΛ^k‖ω‖M(X). So M(homot k F G X) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(δ)·Λ^k·M(X) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(δ)(2Λ)^k M(X).

7. Property (5): boundary commutation and the homotopy formula (Simon 2.24(1), 2.25). Let X ∈ 𝒟_{k+1} be admissible (vanishing off E) with ∂X IM; ∂X vanishes off E too (∂X(ω) = X(dω), tsupport dω ⊆ tsupport ω), so ∂X is admissible. Fix ζ (= 1 near E) and the mollified F_j, G_j.
 (a) Naturality: d(Φ^#ω) = Φ^#(dω) for C^∞ Φ (SimonGMT exteriorDerivativeOn_pullbackFormWithin with U = univ). Since dζ = 0 near E, X(dζ ∧ γ) = 0 for every smooth γ (its tsupport is disjoint from E). Hence ∂X(ζF_j^#ω) = X(d(ζF_j^#ω)) = X(dζ ∧ F_j^#ω) + X(ζF_j^#(dω)) = X(ζF_j^#(dω)). By (Char-push) for ∂X (degree k) and for X (degree k + 1): push k F (∂X)(ω) = lim ∂X(ζF_j^#ω) = lim X(ζF_j^#(dω)) = push (k+1) F X (dω) = (push (k+1) F X).boundary(ω).
 (b) Cartan's homotopy formula for the smooth homotopy h_j (Simon's derivation of 2.25 from 2.21, 2.22 written on forms): for every C^∞ (k+1)-form ω, G_j^#ω − F_j^#ω = d(K_jω) + K_j(dω). Proof: on ℝ × ℝ^P write h_j^#ω = dt ∧ α_t + β_t with α_t, β_t free of dt; then K_jω = ∫_0^1 α_t dt, β_0 = F_j^#ω, β_1 = G_j^#ω, and h_j^#(dω) = d(h_j^#ω) = dt ∧ (∂_tβ_t − d_xα_t) + d_xβ_t, so K_j(dω) = ∫_0^1(∂_tβ_t − d_xα_t) dt = β_1 − β_0 − d(K_jω) (d_x commutes with ∫dt).

 (b) Boundaries: ∂W_0 = ∂T − B_0 − Z_0 = D_0 − Z_0 and ∂W_j = (B_{j−1} + Z_{j−1}) − (B_j + Z_j) = D_j + Z_{j−1} − Z_j (j ≥ 1). These are IM ((IMC)(c), sums and differences of IM currents).
 (c) Z_j vanishes off E_j: Z_0 = D_0 − ∂W_0 and Z_j = D_j + Z_{j−1} − ∂W_j, where W_j, D_j vanish off E_j (so ∂W_j does), and by induction Z_{j−1} vanishes off E_{j−1} ⊆ E_j.
 (d) Σ_{j=0}^{N} W_j = T − A_N, and M(A_N) = μ_T({d < r_N}) ≤ C_Gρ_N^{n+1}M(T) → 0.

6. Deforming the shells (Simon (11)–(20)). For j ≥ 0 let φ_j := φ_{r_j} and Λ_j := Λ(r_j) ≤ c₄2^j; Λ_j ≤ Λ_{j+1}. Then φ_j = ψ on E_j ⊆ {d ≥ r_j}, and φ_{j+1} = φ_j = ψ on E_j. Define (degrees: V_j, W_j ∈ 𝒟_n; H_j ∈ 𝒟_{n+1}; Y_j, L_j ∈ 𝒟_{n−1}; E'_j, K_j ∈ 𝒟_n)
 V_j := push n φ_j W_j, H_j := homot n id φ_j W_j, Y_j := push (n−1) φ_j D_j, E'_j := homot (n−1) id φ_j D_j, L_j := push (n−1) φ_j Z_j, K_j := homot (n−1) id φ_j Z_j.
 All inputs are IM and vanish off the compact E_j, and all maps are Λ_{j+1}-Lipschitz (Λ_j ≤ Λ_{j+1}). By PF:
 - locality: push (n−1) φ_{j+1} Z_j = L_j and homot (n−1) id φ_{j+1} Z_j = K_j (φ_{j+1} = φ_j on E_j);
 - identity and homotopy formula (degree n = (n−1) + 1, F := id, G := φ_j, X := W_j, ∂W_j IM): V_j − W_j − homot (n−1) id φ_j (∂W_j) = ∂H_j;
